Also probing whether you offer a retroactive credit or one-time concession if we pay for the extra capacity as an overage. We can share a usage snapshot (attached) and an internal forecast if that helps.

Two asks: 1) immediate path to lift limits for Nov 27 00:00 PST; 2) outline of commercial impact — what would it cost and any credit options. Procurement is CC'd.

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and the snapshot. Good news: we can provide a short-window rate elevation to prevent throttling. Quick outline below; I put Karthik and Laura on the thread to tee up pricing + contracting so we can move fast.

Plan I'm proposing:
- Temporary lift: raise concurrency and token throughput ceilings for a 72-hour window (Nov 27 00:00 PST to Nov 30 00:00 PST).
- Billing approach: metered overage at a discounted uplift rate (we typically do 1.5x list for short ad-hoc increases).
- Credit concession: because this is a short, customer-impacting event and you are an active commit customer, we can offer a 30% credit on overage invoices for this window if Helpful AI signs the one-off addendum and accepts a short post-event reconciliation (simple true-up).

To proceed we need:
1) Confirmation of estimated peak qps and expected total token delta for the 72-hour window (your forecast or we can accept the snapshot).
2) PO or verbal approval from Procurement so we can stage the change.
3) Signed addendum (attached draft) to authorize the one-off uplift and credit terms.

I've attached a draft addendum that mirrors the outline above. If you confirm numbers now, we can pre-approve the lift and enable it at 00:00 PST on Nov 27.

Attachments: redwood_temp_addendum_draft.pdf

One operational note: we'll enable an automatic rollback policy at the window end. If you need an extension, we should agree terms before the window closes to avoid billing surprises.

—Vanessa Ortiz
